dispatches on dword `[rdx]`: 1 calls `002432B0(rcx+0x50, qword +0x10 of qword 0209AC30, 4, rcx)`, copies the result's words `+4`..`+0xa` to `+0x98`..`+0x9e` when `rcx` is non-null, calls `00247930(rcx, 0x64)` and `00394700(rcx, 3)` and stores word 7 at `+0xc0` and byte 0 at `+0xc2`; 2 acts only when `001EDEC0(dword +0xb4)` and byte `+0xc2` are non-zero: it decrements byte `+0xc2` and, when that reaches 0, reloads bytes `+0xc1`/`+0xc2` from byte tables at image base + `0xbf1720`/`0xbf1728` indexed by the old `+0xc1`, and only for a new `+0xc1` of 3 or 4 sets byte `+0xc3` to 1 or 0 and writes byte `+0xc0` plus 7 (or plus 0) as word `+0xa`, and byte `+7` of that 8-byte entry of its qword `+0x20` as byte `+0x39`, of the object at `[[rcx+0x60]]`; 3 writes words `+0x58`/`+0x5a` of qword `[rcx+0x38]` by byte `+0xc1` (0: 0, 0; 1: ((3 - c2) << 7) / 3, `0xff`; 2: `0x80`, (c2 << 7) / 10 + `0x7f`; 5: `0x80`, ((3 - c2) << 7) / 3 + `0x7f`; 6: (c2 << 7) / 5, `0xff`; else `0x80`, `0x80`; c2 = byte `+0xc2`, low bytes); 0xe stores word `0xa02` at `+0xc1`; 0xf stores word `0x507` at `+0xc0` and byte 3 at `+0xc2`; all these return 0, and any other value tail-jumps to `005C5230(rcx)`

with `B` = qword `+0x10` of `[rdx+0x10]`, stores qword `+0x10` of 0x20-byte entry `r9d` of qword `[rcx+0xc8]` at `B+0x18` and `0020E620(0)` at dword `B+0x20`, and calls `0029FB50(B)`; from the 0x10-byte record at qword `0209AC30` + (`r9d` + 0x6a)*0x20 it keeps word `+8` as `w`, qword `+0` as `p` and byte `+0xa` as `k`, except that when dword `[rcx+0x178]` is `0x402` and word `r9d` of `02B5F210` differs from `w`, `w` becomes that word and `p`, `k` become `002F9860(0x3ea)`, `0xff` when it is `0xffff`, else `002B58B0(qword +0x18 of R, 0)` and byte `R+0x2c` for `R` = `0035D330(1, w << 0x10)`; `D` = qword `+8` of `[rdx+0x10]` gets dword `+0x24` = `002DD7E0(5 if replaced, else 0)`, overwritten by `002DD7E0(4)` when `k` is `0xff`, qword `+0x18` = `p` and dword `+0x20` = `0020E620(0)`; on `[[rdx+0x10]]` it clears bit `0x1` of dword `+8` when `w` is `0xffff`, else writes `k` to word `+0xa` and byte `+7` of 8-byte entry `k` of its qword `+0x20` to byte `+0x39`; returns 1
